sections.body: Vaccine waning models estimate how protection from vaccination declines over time for infections, severe disease, and other outcomes. They sit in epidemiology and population health, within The AI Physician, and they support public health decisions such as booster timing and outbreak planning. These models are population-level tools, not individual clinical predictions. sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on observational data from surveillance systems, cohort studies, test-negative designs, administrative claims, and serological surveys. Analysts typically use statistical software such as R or Python, with Bayesian inference packages for hierarchical models. Large fits may need more memory or compute, but most vaccine waning models do not require specialized hardware. Data linkage and cleaning often take more effort than the modeling itself.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The core task is to estimate a waning curve, which describes how vaccine effectiveness changes with time since vaccination. Common approaches include exponential decay, piecewise functions, splines, and Bayesian hierarchical models that pool information across regions or age groups. Analysts adjust for confounding by calendar time, variant, prior infection, and testing behavior. They validate models with held-out data and sensitivity analyses, then report uncertainty intervals around each estimate.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance matters because these models rely on sensitive health data, so teams document data sources, permissions, and transformations. Reproducibility requires sharing code, model specifications, and assumptions, which helps others audit results. Risks include misreading waning as vaccine failure, which can erode public trust, and overinterpreting sparse data for rare outcomes. The site's 215 compliance and regulation pages reflect the broader attention to privacy, reporting, and oversight in medical AI.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Future work is likely to focus on variant-specific waning, hybrid models that combine trial and real-world data, and better uncertainty quantification. More automated pipelines may speed up updates as new variants emerge, but they will still need careful epidemiological review. Equity in data coverage remains a concern, because some populations are underrepresented in surveillance and cohort studies. As the field matures, vaccine waning models will likely become more integrated with other infectious disease forecasting tools.
